newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin Express sees mutual gain from Sabena.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express sees mutual gain from Sabena.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express no-frills airline said on Thursday that its cooperation with Belgian Sabena provided clear benefits for both carriers.
Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, signed a first commercial agreement with Brussels-based Virgin Express for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow last October.
Sabena, which is taking care of maintenance, ground handling and catering for Virgin Express, has said it is studying more deals on routes from Brussels to Rome, Barcelona and Paris.
"The relationship is clearly mutually beneficial in the areas where we cooperate," Virgin Express chief executive Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters in an interview.

"While we're still competitive in almost all the markets we fly, they are able to help us lower our costs and we help them lower their costs spreading them out over more services such as ground handling," he said.
"Everything we do seems to help Sabena," he said.
But he added that Virgin Express had grown beyond his own expectations in 1996 thanks to the deal with Sabena.
"A large part is result of that deal. The London route is a big addition for us, nine trips a day is a lot of new service," he said.
He added he wanted to solidify Virgin Express's cooperation with Sabena this year.
"We are looking at other opportunities with Sabena," he said without giving further details.
